DEBT Debt consists of the following (in millions, except percentages): Effective Interest Rate As of October 3, 2025 September 27, 2024 1.80% Senior Notes due 2026 1.97 % $ 500.0 $ 500.0 3.00% Senior Notes due 2031 3.13 % 500.0 500.0 Unamortized debt discount and issuance costs ( 4.2 ) ( 5.7 ) Total debt 995.8 994.3 Less: current portion of long-term debt ( 499.4 ) — Total long-term debt $ 496.4 $ 994.3 Senior Notes On May 26, 2021, the Company issued $ 500.0 million of its 0.90 % Senior Notes due 2023 (the “2023 Notes”), $ 500.0 million of its 1.80 % Senior Notes due 2026 (the “2026 Notes”), and $ 500.0 million of its 3.00 % Senior Notes due 2031 (the “2031 Notes” and, together with the 2026 Notes, the “Notes”). During fiscal 2023, the Company repaid $ 500.0 million of the 2023 Notes at maturity. The Notes are senior unsecured obligations of the Company and rank equally in right of payment with all of its existing and future senior unsecured debt but effectively junior to any of the Company’s senior secured debt to the extent of the value of collateral securing such debt and are structurally subordinated to all existing and future obligations of the Company’s subsidiaries. The Notes will mature on each respective maturity date, unless earlier redeemed in accordance with their terms. Interest on the Notes is payable on June 1 and December 1 of each year. The Company may redeem all or a portion of the 2026 Notes and the 2031 Notes at any time and from time to time prior to maturity, in whole or in part, for cash at the applicable redemption prices set forth in the respective supplemental indenture. If the Company undergoes a change of control repurchase event, as defined in the indenture governing the Notes (as supplemented, the “Indenture”), holders may require the Company to repurchase the Notes in whole or in part for cash at a price equal to 101 % of the principal amount of the Notes to be purchased, plus any accrued and unpaid interest. As of October 3, 2025, the Company considered the likelihood of acceleration related to the 2026 Notes and the 2031 Notes and recorded the Notes as short-term debt and long-term debt, respectively. The Notes are recorded net of discount and issuance costs, which are amortized to interest expense over the respective terms of these borrowings.

passages.text: OF OPERATIONS. The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related notes that appear elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. In addition to historical information, the following discussion contains forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ substantially and adversely from those referred to herein due to a number of factors, including, but not limited to, those described below and in Item 1A “Risk Factors” and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. OVERVIEW We, together with our consolidated subsidiaries, are a leading developer, manufacturer and provider of analog and mixed-signal semiconductor products and solutions for numerous applications, including aerospace, automotive, broadband, cellular infrastructure, connected home, defense, entertainment and gaming, industrial, medical, smartphone, tablet, and wearables. Pending Combination With Qorvo On October 27, 2025, we entered into the Merger Agreement with Qorvo, a provider of connectivity and power solutions, to combine Qorvo and Skyworks in a cash-and-stock transaction that values the combined company at approximately $ 22.0 billion as of the market close on October 27, 2025. Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, at the effective time of the Mergers, each share of Qorvo common stock issued and outstanding immediately prior thereto (with certain exceptions set forth in the Merger Agreement) will be converted into the right to receive 0.960 (the “Exchange Ratio”) of a share of Skyworks common stock and $ 32.50 in cash, without interest, subject to applicable withholding taxes. The Exchange Ratio is expected to result in Qorvo equityholders and Skyworks equityholders owning approximately 37% and 63%, respectively, of the combined company on a pro forma basis following the closing. The Merger Agreement also provides for Skyworks’ assumption of certain Qorvo equity awards, subject to certain adjustments thereto in respect of, among other things, performance-based vesting conditions. Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, immediately following the closing, the Board of Directors will be comprised of 11 directors, consisting of (i) the Chief Executive Officer of Skyworks, who will be the Chief Executive Officer of Skyworks following the closing, (ii) seven directors designated by Skyworks and (iii) three directors designated by Qorvo who are reasonably acceptable to Skyworks, each of whom will hold office until the next annual meeting of stockholders of Skyworks. Promptly following the closing, the Board of Directors will also designate a Chairman. Robert Bruggeworth, Qorvo’s current President, Chief Executive Officer and director, will be one of Qorvo’s designees upon the closing. The Mergers, which are anticipated to close early in calendar year 2027, are subject to the satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions, including adoption of the Merger Agreement by Qorvo’s stockholders and the approval by Skyworks’ stockholders of the issuance of Skyworks common stock included in the consideration to

credit_strengths.text: Skyworks generates substantial operating cash flow from its analog and mixed-signal semiconductor franchise, comfortably funding capital expenditure and leaving material free cash flow. This cash generation, paired with a large unrestricted cash balance exceeding total debt, underpins a net cash position and a minimal indicative financial risk profile, well inside sector norms for leverage and cash-flow coverage.

Interest coverage is exceptionally strong, with operating income many times gross interest expense, and the current ratio comfortably exceeds the sector median, reflecting ample near-term liquidity. Gross leverage sits below the sector median, and free cash flow covers debt by a wide margin, supporting a high-quality, investment-grade-like credit profile.

key_risks.text: Revenue and operating income have declined over recent fiscal years, with operating margin now below the sector median, indicating competitive pressure and demand cyclicality in smartphone and broad markets. Continued erosion could weaken cash generation and pressure the credit profile, particularly if capital returns remain elevated relative to free cash flow.

The debt note discloses that the senior notes due in the near term are classified as current, creating a substantial maturity that must be refinanced or repaid. The notes are senior unsecured and structurally subordinated to subsidiary obligations, and a change-of-control repurchase event could require cash redemption, adding refinancing and event risk.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow and free cash flow provide ample coverage of interest and debt, with interest coverage far above the sector median and free cash flow to debt well in excess of one. This capacity is supported by a net cash position, though the upcoming maturity will require refinancing or cash deployment.

Liquidity is strong, with a current ratio above the sector median and cash exceeding total debt. However, shareholder distributions absorb a large share of free cash flow, and the pending Qorvo combination introduces integration and funding considerations that could affect future debt servicing flexibility.

overall_credit_view.text: Skyworks presents a strong credit profile, characterized by net cash, robust interest coverage, and substantial free cash flow. Leverage is below the sector median and the indicative financial risk profile is minimal. The main credit considerations are revenue and margin erosion, the near-term maturity, and the pending Qorvo merger.

We view the credit as resilient, with capacity to absorb cyclical downturns and refinance maturities. The Qorvo combination could alter the risk profile, but current fundamentals and liquidity support a stable outlook. Continued margin pressure and shareholder returns warrant monitoring, yet the net cash position provides a meaningful buffer.

credit_strengths.text: Skyworks 從其類比及混合訊號半導體業務產生龐大營運現金流，足以輕鬆支付資本開支，並留下可觀的自由現金流。此現金產生能力，加上超過總債務的龐大未限制現金結餘，支撐淨現金狀況及極低的指示性財務風險狀況，遠優於行業的槓桿及現金流覆蓋標準。
利息覆蓋率異常強勁，營運收入為總利息開支的許多倍，而流動比率亦遠高於行業中位數，反映短期流動性充裕。總槓桿低於行業中位數，自由現金流大幅覆蓋債務，支持高質量、類投資級的信用狀況。

key_risks.text: 收入及營運收入於最近財政年度下跌，營運利潤率現低於行業中位數，顯示智能手機及廣泛市場的競爭壓力及需求週期性。持續侵蝕可能削弱現金產生能力並對信用狀況構成壓力，尤其是若資本回報相對自由現金流仍維持高企。
債務票據披露，短期內到期的優先票據分類為流動負債，形成須再融資或償還的龐大到期債務。該等票據為優先無抵押，並在結構上次於附屬公司債務，而控制權變更回購事件可能要求現金贖回，增加再融資及事件風險。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營運現金流及自由現金流為利息及債務提供充裕覆蓋，利息覆蓋率遠高於行業中位數，自由現金流對債務比率亦遠超一倍。此能力獲淨現金狀況支持，惟即將到期的債務將需要再融資或動用現金。
流動性強勁，流動比率高於行業中位數，現金超過總債務。然而，股東分派佔用自由現金流的很大部分，而待完成的 Qorvo 合併引入整合及資金考量，可能影響未來債務償付靈活性。

overall_credit_view.text: Skyworks 呈現強勁的信用狀況，其特點為淨現金、穩健的利息覆蓋率及龐大的自由現金流。槓桿低於行業中位數，指示性財務風險狀況為極低。主要信用考量為收入及利潤率侵蝕、短期到期債務，以及待完成的 Qorvo 合併。
我們認為該信用具韌性，有能力吸納週期性低迷及為到期債務再融資。Qorvo 合併可能改變風險狀況，但當前基本面及流動性支持穩定展望。持續的利潤率壓力及股東回報值得監察，惟淨現金狀況提供有意義的緩衝。
